contract: WhyFS 1.0 performance contract, part A: real development workloads, with the measurability rule (BENCHMARK.md section 8)
frozen: 2026-09-28, before the next authoritative run; derived only from pre-existing measurements (results/measurability-calibration.json: 45 historical real-workload measurements, 8 hosted native runs x 4 platforms plus desktop campaigns)
ci: CI90 of the median paired overhead: machine_perf's bootstrap (4000 resamples, seed 1)

rules.PASS: CI90 upper bound < 5 %; or CI90 contains 5 %, CI90 width <= 5 pp and median < 5 %
rules.FAIL: CI90 lower bound >= 5 %; or CI90 contains 5 %, CI90 width <= 5 pp and median >= 5 %
rules.UNMEASURABLE ON THIS RUNNER: CI90 contains 5 % and CI90 width > 5 pp: the measurement cannot resolve the threshold.  Never a PASS; always reported with its raw pairs.

why_width_5pp: A CI90 half-width of at most 2.5 pp (half the budget) bounds the judgment error of a median read against the 5 % threshold to half the budget.  On well-behaved hosted runners 20 pairs give widths of 0.25 to 2.5 pp (60 of 64 hosted measurements <= 5 pp); the noisy exceptions (6.26, 21.6 pp; Windows ARM64 MSVC 7.4 to 14.0 pp in all 8 runs) are the cases the rule must not judge.
why_150_pairs: Resampling each historical measurement's own pairs (scripts/measurability_calibration.py): P(CI90 width <= 5 pp) for Windows ARM64 MSVC is 0.11 at 20 pairs, 0.42 at 60, 0.62 at 100 and 0.79 at 150 (worst historical run 0.56); Windows x64 MSVC reaches >= 0.98 from 100 pairs; Vite and Linux make are >= 0.94 in every historical run from 100 pairs except one pathological Linux x86-64 make run (width 21.6 pp at 20 pairs) that no practical sample resolves.  At the measured ~1.1 min per pair (Windows ARM64) and ~0.95 (Windows x64), 150 pairs keeps every native job within its 330-minute limit (ARM64 about 3.4 h).  Applied to every workload on every platform; fixed before the run, never adapted to the data.
